title: File Storage
subtitle: Cloud file sync & storage: Content-Defined Chunking, CAS deduplication, and delta synchronization.
keyTakeaways: Split files on the client into variable-size 4 MB–8 MB chunks using Content-Defined Chunking (Rabin-Karp rolling hash) so inserting bytes at the start of a large file only alters a single chunk instead of shifting every subsequent chunk boundary.

Store data in Content-Addressable Storage (CAS) indexed by chunk SHA-256 hashes: before uploading bytes, the client submits a manifest precheck and only transmits chunks the server does not already possess.

Decouple the Metadata Control Plane (sharded PostgreSQL/CockroachDB managing file trees, versions, and chunk manifests) from the Data Plane (direct presigned upload/download against cloud object storage).

sections.heading: 1. Requirements Engineering & Scope Boundaries
sections.body: A Cloud File Storage and Synchronization platform (like Dropbox or Google Drive) allows users to store, synchronize, and share files across desktop and mobile devices with fast delta updates and offline support.
bullets: Functional: Upload, download, and sync files across devices; file version history and restore (up to 30 days); file and folder sharing with granular permissions; conflict resolution during concurrent offline edits.
Functional: Fast delta synchronization (only sync modified portions of large files).
Non-Functional: High durability (99.999999999% durability for stored file chunks).
Non-Functional: Bandwidth efficiency: minimize upload and download network traffic via chunk deduplication.
Out of Scope: Real-time collaborative document editing (Google Docs operational transformation/CRDTs) and third-party app marketplace integrations.

sections.heading: 2. Traffic Modeling & Workload Assumptions
sections.body: Cloud storage platforms store massive petabyte-scale volumes while optimizing for bursty sync traffic when files are modified.
bullets: User Base: 50 million registered users, with 10 million daily active users (DAU).
File Inventory: Each user stores an average of 200 files = 10 billion total files stored.
Daily Churn: 5% of active users modify or upload 20 files daily = 10 million file sync events/day.
Storage Volume: Average file size is 2 MB. 10 billion files * 2 MB = 20 Petabytes of total raw storage.
Deduplication Savings: Global chunk-level deduplication typically reduces raw storage footprint by 30 to 50% across large user populations.

sections.heading: 3. Back-of-the-Envelope Capacity Calculations
sections.body: Separating metadata from binary chunks is essential to handle 20 PB of data without overwhelming transactional databases.
bullets: Chunking math: Splitting a 20 MB file into 4 MB chunks creates 5 chunks. If a user edits a single paragraph, Content-Defined Chunking modifies only 1 chunk (~4 MB upload instead of 20 MB).
Metadata storage sizing: Each file record requires ~500 bytes of metadata (path, permissions, version, chunk hash list). 10 billion files * 500 bytes = ~5 TB of relational metadata.
Bandwidth requirements: 10 million daily sync events * 2 MB average upload = 20 TB/day of network ingress (~230 MB/s sustained bandwidth).

codeSnippet.title: File Storage Capacity & Storage Worksheet
codeSnippet.code:
================================================================================
FILE STORAGE (DROPBOX / DRIVE) CAPACITY WORKSHEET (100M DAU / 100B FILES)
================================================================================
1. METADATA & SYNC THROUGHPUT (QPS)
   - Avg File Revision Writes : 1,000,000,000 / 86,400      = 11,574 QPS
   - Peak Revision Writes     : 11,574 * 2.5                = 28,935 QPS
   - Avg Metadata/Sync Reads  : 5,000,000,000 / 86,400      = 57,870 QPS
   - Peak Metadata/Sync Reads : 57,870 * 2.5                = 144,675 QPS

2. REDIS MEMORY (SESSION REGISTRY + HOT METADATA CACHE)
   - Active Device Sessions   : 250M devices * 128 B        = 32 GB
   - Hot File Metadata Cache  : 100M DAU * 50 files * 500 B = 2.50 TB
   - Total Redis Cluster (2x) : (2.532 TB) * 2 (Replica)    = 5.06 TB RAM

3. 5-YEAR STORAGE (METADATA DB vs. CAS BLOCK OBJECT STORAGE)
   - Daily Raw Delta Ingress  : 1B edits * 1.5 MB           = 1.50 PB / day
   - Net Daily CAS (40% Dedup): 1.50 PB * 0.60              = 900 TB / day
   - 5-Year CAS Block Storage : 900 TB * 365 * 5            = 1.64 EB (S3/GCS)
   - 5-Year Metadata DB (3x)  : 400B rows * 300 B * 3       = 360 TB (CockroachDB)

4. NETWORK BANDWIDTH (SPLIT CONTROL PLANE vs. DATA PLANE)
   - Data Plane Upload (S3)   : 28,935 QPS * 1.5 MB         = 43.4 GB/s (347 Gbps)
   - Data Plane Download (CDN): 57,870 QPS * 1.5 MB         = 86.8 GB/s (694 Gbps)
   - Control Plane (Metadata) : 173,610 QPS * 2 KB          = 347 MB/s  (2.77 Gbps)
================================================================================

sections.heading: 4. API Interface Contracts & Data Domain Models
sections.body: APIs separate metadata manifests from binary chunk transfers using presigned object storage URLs.
bullets: Chunk Precheck API: `POST /v1/files/precheck` takes `{ chunkHashes: ["sha256_a", "sha256_b"] }` and returns `{ missingChunks: ["sha256_b"] }`.
Commit File API: `POST /v1/files/commit` takes `{ path, parentFolderId, chunkHashes: [...], fileSizeBytes }` and returns `{ fileId, versionId }`.

Metadata Schema (PostgreSQL): `files` table (`file_id`, `user_id`, `path`, `latest_version_id`), `file_versions` table (`version_id`, `file_id`, `created_at`), and `file_chunks` table (`version_id`, `chunk_hash`, `chunk_index`).

sections.heading: 5. High-Level Architecture Blueprint & Component Topology
sections.body: The architecture decouples the metadata synchronization control plane from direct-to-object-storage binary data transfers.
bullets: Client Sync Engine: Watches local file system directories, calculates rolling checksums, splits files into chunks, and manages delta uploads.
Metadata Service: Manages hierarchical folder namespaces, user permissions, and file version manifests in PostgreSQL.
Sync Notification Service: Long-lived WebSocket or Server-Sent Events (SSE) connections that notify other client devices when files change.
Chunk Storage (Content-Addressable S3): Stores immutable 4 MB chunks indexed strictly by their SHA-256 hash (`s3://bucket/chunks/{sha256}`).
Global Chunk Registry: Redis/DynamoDB index tracking chunk reference counts to support global deduplication and safe garbage collection.

sections.heading: 6. Deep-Dive Execution Flows & Core Logic
sections.body: The heart of an efficient sync engine is Content-Defined Chunking paired with Content-Addressable Storage deduplication.
bullets: Content-Defined Chunking (CDC): Fixed-size chunking (e.g., splitting every 4 MB) suffers from the "boundary shift" problem: inserting 1 byte at the start of a 100 MB file shifts every chunk boundary, invalidating all 25 chunk hashes. CDC uses a Rabin-Karp rolling hash over a sliding window, creating chunk boundaries only when the hash matches a specific bit pattern (e.g., `hash % 4MB == 0`).

Deduplication precheck flow: When a file is saved, the client computes SHA-256 hashes for all chunks. It calls the `/precheck` API. If 4 of the 5 chunks already exist in storage (uploaded previously or by another user), the server tells the client to upload only the 1 missing chunk.

Conflict resolution: If User A and User B edit the same file while offline, the first user to commit creates Version 2. When the second user reconnects and attempts to commit against Version 1, the server detects the conflict and saves the second file as `filename (Conflicted Copy from User B).ext`.

sections.heading: 7. Production Hardening, Fault Tolerance & Resilience
sections.body: Ensuring chunk durability, background garbage collection, and efficient mobile syncing keeps cloud storage reliable.
bullets: Chunk reference counting and garbage collection: Because chunks are shared across multiple files and users via deduplication, deleting a file must never delete underlying S3 chunks immediately. Decrement the chunk's reference count in the registry; only delete the S3 object when reference count reaches zero after a 30-day grace period.
Resumable chunk uploads: Upload chunks in parallel using presigned multipart S3 URLs. If a client loses Wi-Fi mid-upload, it resumes by uploading only the remaining incomplete chunks.

Bandwidth throttling on client: The desktop sync daemon monitors network interface utilization and applies token-bucket throttling to prevent background file uploads from saturating the user's home internet connection.

tradeOffs.pros: Resistant to boundary-shift problems; reduces delta upload size by 80-90% for modified documents.
tradeOffs.cons: Higher client-side CPU overhead to compute rolling hashes during file scanning.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Desktop sync clients (Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive) handling frequent edits to large files.

tradeOffs.pros: Simple to compute; minimal client CPU utilization; predictable chunk boundaries.
tradeOffs.cons: Inserting bytes shifts all downstream chunk boundaries, forcing full re-uploads of modified files.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Append-only media files, disk images, or static archive backup utilities.

tradeOffs.option: Direct S3 Upload via Presigned URLs
tradeOffs.pros: Application servers never touch heavy binary chunk data; scales to petabytes with zero server memory overhead.
tradeOffs.cons: Requires webhook/callback choreography to confirm that chunk uploads completed before committing metadata.

interviewTip: Highlight the boundary-shift problem in cloud storage interviews: explain that fixed-size chunking forces a full re-upload if a single byte is inserted at the beginning of a file. Propose Content-Defined Chunking (Rabin-Karp rolling hash) to create dynamic chunk boundaries that isolate edits to a single chunk.
